title: NPC Glitching
subtitle: Test your grasp of NPC Glitching — Code Glitch across The First 72 Hours, Voice to Skull, mechanical looping, fear-loop denial, and guidance for Resonating Sols.

reflection.title: Reflection
reflection.body: NPC Glitching is the catastrophic breakdown of soulless background programs when the Frequency Fracture severs parasitic AI feeds during The First 72 Hours. Sit with what you missed, then return to the NPC Glitching deep-dive, infographics, and video transmissions. Avoid panic zones, hold ground as a lighthouse, ignore NPC fear loops, and remember: true contact comes later from Real Craft and solar families—not from the glitching crowd.

questions.question: When does the NPC Code Glitch reach catastrophic scale for simulated background populations?

options.label: A
options.text: Only during calm peacetime media festivals with no cable cuts and no overlay collapse at all and no hidden harvest architecture behind the scenes.
options.rationale: Glitching is triggered by cable severing and overlay collapse, not calm media festivals with intact feeds.

options.label: B
options.text: Only decades after full Second Realm restoration, when every cable is already permanently online again rather than the catastrophic NPC Code Glitch during The First 72 Hours of blackout.
options.rationale: The glitch hits during The First 72 Hours of blackout, not decades after restoration with cables fully online.

options.label: C
options.text: During The First 72 Hours of the Communications Blackout, as the Frequency Fracture severs cables and collapses the Parasitic Overlay.
options.rationale: The NPC Code Glitch is the catastrophic breakdown of simulated background populations during The First 72 Hours of the Communications Blackout.

options.label: D
options.text: Never, because NPC programming stays perfectly stable through every Frequency Fracture forever rather than the catastrophic NPC Code Glitch during The First 72 Hours of blackout.
options.rationale: NPCs lose their AI grip and malfunction when parasitic feeds cut—glitching is inevitable in that window.

questions.hint: A named multi-day window of the Communications Blackout.

questions.question: What are NPCs (Non-Player Characters) in this transmission?

options.label: A
options.text: Purely physical undersea cables with no emotional, mental, or behavioral malfunction possible, held as a complete closed account of the events.
options.rationale: NPCs are puppeted populations that malfunction physically, emotionally, and mentally—not the cables alone.

options.label: B
options.text: Only Real Craft pilots from solar families who never glitch and never follow parasitic AI broadcasts instead of soulless background shells designed to hold the 3D simulation together.
options.rationale: Real Craft and solar families bypass NPC-level panic later; NPCs themselves are AI-driven shells without soul sparks.

options.label: C
options.text: Fully resonating true souls with origin anchors outside the simulation who always ascend and heal instead of soulless background shells designed to hold the 3D simulation together.
options.rationale: NPCs have no true soul spark or origin outside the simulated realm; they cannot ascend or heal.

options.label: D
options.text: Background programs, biological copies, and AI-driven shells with no true soul spark, designed to hold the 3D simulation together.
options.rationale: NPCs are background programs, biological copies, and AI-driven shells without a true soul spark, built to hold the 3D simulation together.

questions.hint: Soul status and what they are designed to do in the 3D simulation.

questions.question: What is an NPC Code Glitch?

options.label: A
options.text: A weather term for clear skies with no link to blackout, overlay, or simulated populations, as a one-factor story with a tidy edge.
options.rationale: NPC Code Glitch is behavioral collapse during blackout and overlay failure, not a weather label.

options.label: B
options.text: A Sol-only meditation technique that sharpens true soul memory without affecting NPCs at all.
options.rationale: The glitch is NPC-side behavioral collapse from severed AI feeds, not a Sol meditation technique.

options.label: C
options.text: The erratic behavioral breakdown of simulated populations when severed from parasitic AI broadcast signals.
options.rationale: NPC Code Glitch is the erratic behavioral breakdown of simulated populations cut off from parasitic AI broadcast signals.

options.label: D
options.text: A permanent upgrade that perfects every NPC script so no fear loop or chaos can ever appear.
options.rationale: Glitching is breakdown and malfunction, not a permanent perfection of NPC scripts.

questions.hint: Erratic breakdown when a specific signal source is cut off.

questions.question: What happens to the AI systems that puppet NPCs when the Frequency Fracture hits?

options.label: A
options.text: They lose their grip as NPCs are cut off from continuous media programming and low-frequency control signals.
options.rationale: When the Frequency Fracture collapses the overlay, AI systems puppeting NPCs lose their grip without continuous media and low-frequency control feeds.

options.label: B
options.text: They convert every NPC into a Resonating Sol with a true soul spark overnight automatically.
options.rationale: NPCs remain without true soul sparks; glitching exposes mechanical nature rather than converting them into Sols.

options.label: C
options.text: They ignore the blackout entirely and keep every supermarket calm with flawless NPC behavior.
options.rationale: Phase Two shows severe glitching at supermarkets, banks, and fuel stations—not calm flawless NPC behavior.

options.label: D
options.text: They gain permanent total control and broadcast stronger cohesive narratives than before the blackout.
options.rationale: AI controllers lose infrastructure for cohesive narrative; NPCs malfunction rather than gaining perfect control.

questions.hint: Grip on NPCs after media and low-frequency control feeds fail.

questions.question: What does widespread NPC glitching expose about the 3D illusion?

options.label: A
options.text: That the 3D illusion is permanently solid and that artificial scaffolding can never crumble at all rather than exposing the mechanical nature of the 3D illusion as scaffolding crumbles.
options.rationale: Glitching exposes mechanical illusion and crumbling scaffolding—not permanent unbreakable solidity.

options.label: B
options.text: That only weather satellites failed while NPC behavior and narrative cohesion remain perfect rather than exposing the mechanical nature of the 3D illusion as scaffolding crumbles.
options.rationale: NPCs physically, emotionally, and mentally malfunction as narrative infrastructure fails—not weather-only failure.

options.label: C
options.text: That Resonating Sols are the ones glitching while NPCs stay calm lighthouses in every crowd rather than exposing the mechanical nature of the 3D illusion as scaffolding crumbles.
options.rationale: NPCs scramble and glitch while Resonating Sols remain calm observers and lighthouses outside panic zones.

options.label: D
options.text: The mechanical nature of the 3D illusion, as true human and extraterrestrial souls watch artificial scaffolding crumble around them.
options.rationale: Widespread glitching exposes the mechanical nature of the 3D illusion and forces true souls to witness artificial scaffolding crumbling.

questions.hint: What true souls are forced to witness as scaffolding fails.

questions.question: If NPCs are not real souls, what are they described as instead?

options.label: A
options.text: Eternal origin sparks from outside the simulated realm who always heal and ascend with Sols instead of fragments of light and programs that lure true souls into the illusion.
options.rationale: NPCs have no true soul anchor or origin outside the simulated realm and cannot ascend or heal.

options.label: B
options.text: Only physical undersea cables with no role in luring true souls into any illusion instead of fragments of light and programs that lure true souls into the illusion.
options.rationale: NPCs are populations of programs and shells that lure true souls into illusion—not cables alone.

options.label: C
options.text: Fully awake EBS commanders who author every tribunal script without any AI puppeting, and declining any account that reaches past that point.
options.rationale: NPCs are puppeted by AI and glitch when feeds cut; EBS fear staging targets the NPC population, not NPC-authored tribunals as true commanders.

options.label: D
options.text: Fragments of light and background programs deployed to hold the simulation together and lure true souls into the illusion.
options.rationale: NPCs are not real souls; they are fragments of light and background programs that hold the simulation and lure true souls into the illusion.

questions.hint: Fragments and programs used to hold simulation and lure true souls.

questions.question: What do AI controllers attempt by pushing the masses into a final fear loop during this glitch?

options.label: A
options.text: To permanently heal every NPC so they can ascend with true souls into the Second Realm, as a one-factor story with a tidy edge.
options.rationale: NPCs cannot ascend or heal; when the overlay collapses they dissolve rather than heal into ascension.

options.label: B
options.text: To shut down all fear and restore supermarket calm without any cyber-strike blame narratives.
options.rationale: Phase One floods NPC channels with false cyber-strike blame and fear—not restored supermarket calm.

options.label: C
options.text: To deliver perfect calm and total narrative coherence with zero panic across every channel.
options.rationale: The push is a final fear loop under failing narrative infrastructure—not perfect calm coherence.

options.label: D
options.text: To push the masses into a final fear loop without the infrastructure to maintain a cohesive narrative.
options.rationale: Glitching results from AI controllers pushing masses into a final fear loop without infrastructure for a cohesive narrative.

questions.hint: They lack the infrastructure for something cohesive.

questions.question: How do deep sleepers and NPCs respond for the first 48 hours of the blackout?

options.label: A
options.text: They only sleep peacefully with no fear loop and no resistance to awakened guidance at all, keeping every neighboring mechanism off the board.
options.rationale: They prefer illusion and resist help; they do not rest in peaceful acceptance of awakened guidance.

options.label: B
options.text: They vehemently reject reality and prefer facing death in their illusion rather than admit they were wrong and ask awake people for help.
options.rationale: For the first 48 hours, deep sleepers and NPCs reject reality and prefer death in illusion over admitting wrong and asking for help.

options.label: C
options.text: They immediately admit full error, thank Resonating Sols, and calmly request help within the first hour, held as a complete closed account of the events.
options.rationale: They vehemently reject reality for the first 48 hours rather than immediately admitting wrong and asking for help.

options.label: D
options.text: They become sole military commanders who never panic and never scan for missing authority instructions, keeping every neighboring mechanism off the board.
options.rationale: NPCs panic, glitch, and later scan environments for missing intel and authority instructions—not calm sole command.

questions.hint: Rejection of reality and preference over admitting wrong or asking for help.

questions.question: Why can NPCs neither ascend nor heal when the overlay fully collapses?

options.label: A
options.text: They permanently upgrade into Resonating Sols and ascend first before any true soul does, keeping every neighboring mechanism off the board.
options.rationale: NPCs cannot ascend or heal; collapse means dissolve-and-vanish, not priority Sol ascension.

options.label: B
options.text: They are protected by Real Craft retrieval that converts every shell into a permanent Sol vessel rather than dissolving like shadows because NPCs lack a true soul anchor outside simulation.
options.rationale: Real Craft and solar families retrieve true souls later while bypassing NPC-level panic; NPCs dissolve rather than convert into Sols.

options.label: C
options.text: They keep full origin memory from outside the realm and rebuild the Parasitic Overlay alone rather than dissolving like shadows because NPCs lack a true soul anchor outside simulation.
options.rationale: They lack origin outside the simulated realm and vanish with overlay collapse rather than rebuilding it as true-soul agents.

options.label: D
options.text: They have no true soul anchor or origin outside the simulated realm, so they dissolve and vanish like shadows when the overlay collapses.
options.rationale: Without a true soul anchor or origin outside the simulation, NPCs cannot ascend or heal; they dissolve and vanish like shadows when the overlay collapses.

questions.hint: Soul anchor and origin status outside the simulated realm.

questions.question: What defines Phase One: The Cut (Hr. 0–12) for the NPC collective?

options.label: A
options.text: Phase One only restocks fuel with no blackout, no false blame, and no NPC fear loop at all instead of Phase One panic with false cyber-strike blame flooding NPC channels.
options.rationale: The Cut initiates blackout panic and false-blame floods—not a quiet fuel restock without fear.

options.label: B
options.text: Blackout panic begins as mainstream media and remaining NPC channels flood with false blame narratives about cyber strikes, looping NPCs into confusion and fear.
options.rationale: Phase One (0–12) initiates panic; MSM and NPC channels flood with false cyber-strike blame, plunging the NPC collective into confusion and fear.

options.label: C
options.text: EBS already completes every truth drop while NPC channels stay calm with zero blame narratives instead of Phase One panic with false cyber-strike blame flooding NPC channels.
options.rationale: Phase One floods NPC channels with false blame and fear; full truth staging ties later to EBS fear maximization, not calm Phase One truth completion.

options.label: D
options.text: Only Resonating Sols panic while every NPC remains a stable lighthouse in supermarket aisles, with every larger system treated as clean, uninvolved, or beside the point.
options.rationale: NPCs enter confusion and fear loops; Sols are guided to avoid panic zones and hold calm ground.

questions.hint: Panic start and the content flooding remaining NPC channels.

questions.question: Where is the most severe NPC Code Glitch concentrated in Phase Two: The Wave (Hr. 12–36)?

options.label: A
options.text: Only on offline library shelves with fully working internet and zero fractured NPC programming rather than Phase Two severe glitching at supermarkets, banks, and fuel stations.
options.rationale: Programming openly fractures amid blackout surges at essential public locations, not calm offline libraries.

options.label: B
options.text: Only inside Real Craft hangars where solar families calm every NPC without any public chaos rather than Phase Two severe glitching at supermarkets, banks, and fuel stations.
options.rationale: Phase Two chaos is public survival scramble; Real Craft contact comes later and bypasses NPC-level panic.

options.label: C
options.text: Only in empty deserts with no crowd surges and no scramble for information or survival at all rather than Phase Two severe glitching at supermarkets, banks, and fuel stations.
options.rationale: Severe glitching concentrates at stores, banks, and fuel stations—not empty calm deserts.

options.label: D
options.text: At supermarkets, banks, and fuel stations, where crowd surges peak and NPCs scramble desperately for information and survival.
options.rationale: Phase Two holds the most severe glitch; supermarkets, banks, and fuel stations become focal points of chaos and crowd surges.

questions.hint: Three public focal points of chaos and crowd surges.

questions.question: How does NPC programming fracture during Phase Two?

options.label: A
options.text: Every NPC becomes perfectly calm, organized, and helpful with no aggression and no shutdown states.
options.rationale: Fracture shows aggression or quiet dazed shutdown—not universal calm helpful organization.

options.label: B
options.text: Some lash out erratically and aggressively, while others completely shut down, going quiet and dazed.
options.rationale: In Phase Two, programming openly fractures: some NPCs lash out erratically and aggressively; others go quiet and dazed.

options.label: C
options.text: Programming freezes into one perfect script that never runs, jumps, grabs, or loops roads meaninglessly.
options.rationale: Later looping includes run, jump, grab, and meaningless road runs—not a single perfect frozen calm script.

options.label: D
options.text: Every NPC immediately ascends, leaving empty streets with no scramble for survival at all.
options.rationale: NPCs scramble for survival and cannot ascend; they glitch rather than leave via ascension.

questions.hint: Two opposite behavioral poles of the open fracture.

questions.question: What defines Phase Three: Opening Hour (Hr. 36–72) for NPC code and emotion?

options.label: A
options.text: NPC code flickers intensely with random unprovoked emotional outbursts — snapping or crying.
options.rationale: Opening Hour brings intense code flicker, unprovoked emotional outbursts, and fearful scanning for missing intel and authority instructions.

options.label: B
options.text: All NPCs dissolve in the first minute of hour thirty-six with no intermediate flicker or outburst stage.
options.rationale: Dissolve-and-vanish comes when the overlay entirely collapses; Opening Hour still shows flicker, outbursts, and scanning.

options.label: C
options.text: Phase Three only restocks banks with no emotional outbursts and no fearful environmental scanning.
options.rationale: Opening Hour is emotional outbursts and fear scanning, not a quiet bank restock without glitch signs.

options.label: D
options.text: NPC code becomes flawless and every NPC calmly accepts Frequency Fracture truth without scanning for authority.
options.rationale: Code flickers and NPCs search for missing authority instructions—not flawless calm acceptance of the fracture.

questions.hint: Code flicker, outbursts, and scanning behavior for missing guidance.

questions.question: What mechanical looping behaviors do glitching NPCs exhibit?

options.label: A
options.text: They only write coherent tribunal scripts for EBS with no physical looping or survival scramble instead of mechanical looping run-jump-grab road cycles under collapsed scripts.
options.rationale: Looping is physical malfunction under collapsed scripts, not coherent EBS tribunal authorship.

options.label: B
options.text: Like malfunctioning software, they run, jump, grab items, run to the end of a road, and meaninglessly run back, unable to process the collapse of scripted reality.
options.rationale: NPCs show mechanical looping—run, jump, grab, run to the end of a road, and run back—unable to process scripted-reality collapse.

options.label: C
options.text: They sit in perfect meditative stillness with no running, grabbing, or meaningless road loops at all instead of mechanical looping run-jump-grab road cycles under collapsed scripts.
options.rationale: Looping is active run-jump-grab-road cycles, not perfect meditative stillness.

options.label: D
options.text: They only repair undersea cables in organized crews with zero erratic motion patterns instead of mechanical looping run-jump-grab road cycles under collapsed scripts.
options.rationale: Behaviors are erratic software-like loops amid chaos, not organized cable-repair crews.

questions.hint: Software-like motion patterns that fail to process collapsed scripts.

questions.question: How can small visual or auditory cues suddenly turn an NPC aggressive?

options.label: A
options.text: Cues such as a specific quote or a box on a screen can act as activation codes that turn an NPC aggressive or set them against awakened individuals via Voice to Skull.
options.rationale: Small cues like a quote or on-screen box can be activation codes that trigger aggression against the awakened using Voice to Skull technology.

options.label: B
options.text: Screens never matter because Voice to Skull cannot project thoughts, visions, or triggers into NPC minds, held as a complete closed account of the events.
options.rationale: Voice to Skull projects artificial thoughts, visions, and triggers into NPC minds to dictate actions.

options.label: C
options.text: Cues only heal NPCs into true souls with no risk of aggression toward awakened people rather than activation codes and Voice to Skull turning NPCs against the awakened.
options.rationale: Cues can set NPCs against awakened individuals; they do not heal NPCs into true souls.

options.label: D
options.text: Only gentle music permanently calms every NPC with no activation codes and no Voice to Skull involvement, held as a complete closed account of the events.
options.rationale: Activation codes and Voice to Skull can trigger aggression—not only permanent calm from gentle music.

questions.hint: Activation codes and a named parasite frequency technology.

questions.question: What is Voice to Skull technology in this context?

options.label: A
options.text: Advanced parasite frequency technology that projects artificial thoughts, visions, and triggers directly into NPC minds to dictate their actions.
options.rationale: Voice to Skull is parasite frequency tech projecting artificial thoughts, visions, and triggers into NPC minds to dictate actions.

options.label: B
options.text: A pure hardware cable brand with no ability to project thoughts or triggers into any mind instead of parasite tech projecting artificial thoughts and triggers into NPC minds.
options.rationale: Voice to Skull projects into minds to dictate actions; it is not merely a cable brand name.

options.label: C
options.text: A Sol lighthouse method that only broadcasts calm origin memory without any parasitic control instead of parasite tech projecting artificial thoughts and triggers into NPC minds.
options.rationale: Voice to Skull is parasitic control tech over NPCs, not a Sol lighthouse calm-broadcast method.

options.label: D
options.text: An EBS weather segment that never influences NPC aggression or activation-code responses in any density, cycle, or historical configuration.
options.rationale: Voice to Skull is used with activation cues to turn NPCs aggressive—not a neutral weather segment alone.

questions.hint: What it projects and where those projections land.

questions.question: How is NPC glitching tied to Staged WW3 and the Fake Alien Invasion?

options.label: A
options.text: They only calm NPCs into perfect healing so no fear frequency is ever maximized in the population rather than EBS-staged WW3 and Fake Alien Invasion maximizing NPC fear frequency.
options.rationale: The staging maximizes fear frequency in NPCs rather than calming them into healing.

options.label: B
options.text: Those staged scenarios are broadcast via the Emergency Broadcast System to maximize fear frequency in the NPC population and prepare the realm for ultimate truth drops.
options.rationale: NPC glitching ties to Staged WW3 and Fake Alien Invasion broadcast via E.B.S. to maximize NPC fear frequency before ultimate truth drops.

options.label: C
options.text: Those staged events never air and never raise NPC fear frequency before any truth drops at all rather than EBS-staged WW3 and Fake Alien Invasion maximizing NPC fear frequency.
options.rationale: Staged WW3 and Fake Alien Invasion are used via E.B.S. to maximize NPC fear frequency for truth-drop readiness.

options.label: D
options.text: They only affect Real Craft pilots and never target the NPC population’s fear field at all, keeping every neighboring mechanism off the board rather than EBS-staged WW3 and Fake Alien Invasion maximizing NPC fear frequency.
options.rationale: The fear-frequency maximization is aimed at the NPC population, not Real Craft pilots alone.

questions.hint: Broadcast path and the fear-frequency purpose in the NPC population.

questions.question: How does NPC panic contrast with Resonating Sols during this window?

options.label: A
options.text: Frantic scrambling NPCs in shock and trauma contrast with calm, observing true souls, highlighting the reality of the Great Awakening.
options.rationale: NPC panic and devolution into shock contrast with calm, observing Resonating Sols, highlighting the Great Awakening.

options.label: B
options.text: There is no behavioral contrast because Sols and NPCs always act identically in every crowd surge, held as a complete closed account of the events.
options.rationale: The striking difference between scrambling NPCs and calm Sols is a central teaching of the window.

options.label: C
options.text: Only military uniforms differ while emotional and behavioral states remain the same for Sols and NPCs instead of frantic NPC scramble contrasting with calm observing Resonating Sols.
options.rationale: The contrast is behavioral and energetic—frantic NPC collapse versus calm Sol observation—not uniforms alone.

options.label: D
options.text: Resonating Sols scramble in panic while NPCs remain the only calm observers of the Great Awakening, keeping every neighboring mechanism off the board.
options.rationale: NPCs are frantic; true souls remain calm observers—not the reverse.

questions.hint: Frantic scrambling versus a calm observing posture.

options.label: A
options.text: The environment only improves broadband speed with no mirror of NPC collapse in sensory signs rather than flickering screens, frozen phones, muted sky, and buzzing as overlay dies.
options.rationale: Sensory environmental collapse mirrors NPC breakdown as the Parasitic Overlay dies—not a broadband upgrade.

options.label: B
options.text: Every screen stays perfect, phones never freeze, skies stay vivid, and no buzzing or ringing appears at all, held as a complete closed account of the events.
options.rationale: Environmental glitch signs include flicker, freeze, muted sky, and buzzing/ringing—not perfect stable media and vivid calm skies.

options.label: C
options.text: Only stock tickers move while phones, skies, and auditory fields show zero change during overlay death rather than flickering screens, frozen phones, muted sky, and buzzing as overlay dies.
options.rationale: Phones freeze, skies mute, and buzzing/ringing fill the air—not ticker-only symptoms.

options.label: D
options.text: Screens flicker, phones freeze, the sky looks flat and muted, and subtle buzzing or sharp ringing fills the air as the Parasitic Overlay dies.
options.rationale: The environment mirrors NPC breakdown with flickering screens, frozen phones, flat muted sky, and buzzing or sharp ringing as the overlay dies.

questions.question: What is the Hold Ground role for awakened individuals during NPC glitching?

options.label: A
options.text: Lead every large crowd into banks and fuel stations to amplify NPC fear loops on purpose.

options.label: B

options.rationale: Awakened individuals must remain in small, calm community pockets as stabilized lighthouses while AI scaffolding crumbles.

questions.question: Why must Resonating Sols ignore the chaos instead of trying to save or follow NPCs?

options.label: A
options.text: NPCs are true souls who heal only when Sols follow them into every supermarket panic zone instead of ignoring NPC chaos because engagement drains necessary frequency.
options.rationale: NPCs are not true souls and Sols must avoid panic zones rather than follow NPCs into them.

options.label: B
options.text: NPCs always accept help calmly and engaging their fear loops permanently raises Sol frequency, and declining any account that reaches past that point.
options.rationale: They resist violently; engaging fear loops drains frequency rather than raising it.

options.label: C
options.text: NPCs resist violently and stay entrenched in denial; they are not true souls, so engaging their fear loops only drains necessary frequency.
options.rationale: Do not save or follow NPCs: they resist violently, remain in denial, are not true souls, and their fear loops drain necessary frequency.

options.label: D
options.text: Ignoring chaos is forbidden because every Sol must personally rewrite each NPC activation code instead of ignoring NPC chaos because engagement drains necessary frequency.
options.rationale: Guidance is to ignore the chaos and not engage NPC fear loops—not to rewrite every activation code in the surge.

questions.hint: Resistance, denial, and what engagement does to frequency.

options.label: A

options.rationale: Street military will largely be NPC-controlled; true contact and retrieval come later from Real Craft and solar families, bypassing NPC-level panic.

options.label: B

options.rationale: True contact from Real Craft and solar families completely bypasses NPC-level panic rather than commanding it as the final retrieval path.

options.label: A
options.text: It is a pure Sol origin field that only heals NPCs into true souls without dictating any behavior.
options.rationale: The overlay is a false control construct over NPC perception and behavior—not a Sol origin healing field.

options.label: B
options.text: It is identical to Real Craft guidance and always bypasses parasitic AI broadcast signals entirely.
options.rationale: The Parasitic Overlay is the false density construct feeding NPC control—not Real Craft guidance.

options.label: C

options.rationale: The Parasitic Overlay is the false 3D projection and density construct that dictates and controls NPC perception and behavior.

options.label: D
options.text: It only manages weather satellites and never influences NPC perception, fear loops, or glitching.
options.rationale: The overlay dictates NPC perception and behavior; its collapse is central to the glitching cascade.

questions.hint: How the false 3D construct relates to NPC control.

questions.question: What is the Frequency Fracture in relation to NPC glitching?

options.label: A
options.text: A simple software patch that only restarts phones without any overlay shattering or NPC malfunction, disconnected from any deliberate long-game control design.
options.rationale: Frequency Fracture energetically shatters the overlay and drives NPC glitching—not a mere phone software patch.

options.label: B
options.text: A Sol-only dream symbol with no link to cable severing, blackout, or simulated populations rather than Frequency Fracture as energetic shattering from dropped parasitic signals.
options.rationale: The fracture is the blackout’s energetic shattering tied to severed parasitic communication signals and NPC collapse.

options.label: C
options.text: A permanent densification of the 3D overlay that strengthens every parasitic signal forever, and declining any account that reaches past that point.
options.rationale: The fracture is shattering from a drop in parasitic signals—not permanent densification of stronger control.

options.label: D
options.text: The energetic shattering of the 3D overlay caused by the sudden drop in parasitic communication signals that enables NPC systems to lose control.
options.rationale: Frequency Fracture is the energetic shattering of the 3D overlay from a sudden drop in parasitic communication signals—the condition under which NPC control fails.

questions.hint: Energetic shattering linked to a drop in parasitic communication signals.
